FINDINGS:

Fractures:
Known mildly comminuted undisplaced avulsion fracture of the tibial tuberosity involving the distal ACL insertion, anteriorly the anterior horn root insertion of the lateral meniscus, as well as posteriorly the tibial insertion of both the posterior horn of medial and lateral menisci. The fracture involves the central portion of the medial tibial plateau articular surface anteriorly and posteriorly with articular surface collapse of 3 mm anteriorly and 5 mm posteriorly, as well as a step deformity of up to 2 mm posteriorly.
Small mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the lateral corner of lateral tibial plateau [Segond fracture].
Small mild osteochondral impaction at the anterior lateral weightbearing aspect of lateral femoral condyle.
There is associated bone marrow edema associated with these fractures.

Joint alignment:
Mild widening of the medial femorotibial joint space. Otherwise preserved articular alignment.

Degenerative changes:
None.

Bone marrow signal:
Additional small area of bone marrow edema on the medial side of medial femoral condyle without evidence of associated fracture.

Anterior cruciate ligament: The distal bony avulsion with laxity of the ACL, showing some internal high T2 signal changes compatible with additional low-grade partial ligamentous tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament: Intact with mild laxity.
Medial collateral ligament: Complete tear of the superficial portion at the mid to distal third. Moderate grade partial tear of the deep meniscal femoral and meniscal tibial components with partial meniscocapsular separation of the medial meniscal body.
Lateral collateral ligament complex: Low-grade sprain of the proximal lateral collateral ligament. The other associated structures are intact.

Medial meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes of the meniscal body, with evidence of small horizontal oblique tear extending to the femoral surface. No other significant tear. Bony avulsion of the posterior horn root insertion as detailed above.
Lateral meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes at the anterior horn compatible with low-grade tearing. Evidence of small Wrisberg rip-type longitudinal tear of the periphery of the posterior horn. Complete tear of the inferior meniscal popliteal fascicle compatible with posterior lateral corner injury. There is a bony avulsion of the anterior horn and posterior horn root insertion sites.

Extensor tendons: Normal.
Patellar retinacula: Moderate grade partial tear of the medial retinaculum.
Pes anserinus: Normal.

Posteromedial and posterolateral corner: Diffuse signal change and mild thickening of the distal semimembranosus tendon compatible with low to moderate grade partial tearing.
Complete tear of the inferior meniscal popliteal fascicle compatible with posterior lateral corner injury.

Joint effusion: Large joint effusion.
Baker cyst: None.

Other significant findings:
None.

CONCLUSION:
*Comminuted mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the tibial spine with mild comminution, including the distal insertion of the ACL, the anterior horn root insertion of the lateral meniscus, and posterior horn root insertion zone of the medial and lateral menisci. Intra-articular fracture extension involving the central portion of the medial tibial plateau with small gap/step as described.
*Small mildly displaced lateral corner fracture of the lateral tibial plateau [Segond fracture].
*Small osteochondral impaction fracture of the lateral corner of lateral femoral condyle.
*High-grade tear of the medial collateral ligament.
*Low-grade partial tear/sprain of the anterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament.
*Additional low-grade tears involving the medial and lateral menisci as described.
*Moderate grade partial tear of the medial patellar retinaculum.
*Posteromedial and posterolateral corner injuries as described.
*Large joint effusion.
